# A whole persists through the generation of its parts

<!-- Generated by build_result_registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

> Where parts are brief, or end with finitely many active at once, a persisting whole needs its parts to keep arising.

`whole-persists-through-generation` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01

<a id="主张-claim"></a>
## Claim

On webs, a formation is the whole of some parts when it is active exactly while some part is. A whole arises only as some part arises, so where a whole arises at arbitrarily late steps its parts do too. This is coincidence of activity, not constitution: every formation is the whole of itself, and two formations active at every step are each the whole of the other (whole_self, Immortal.each_other). Where parts cover every step from some step on, some part being active at each: if no part is active at two steps d apart, no d consecutive steps from that step on pass with no part arising; if every part's activity ends and at each step a finite list names exactly the active parts, no step is followed only by steps at which no part arises, nor only by steps at which no part outside a given finite list arises: that ever new parts arise cannot be refuted (Covered.arises_within, Covered.needs_arising, Covered.needs_new). A whole active at every step from some step on is covered by its parts (Whole.covered), so it persists only through the unceasing generation of its parts. Under Brief this may be the same parts arising again (Layered: both members are Brief 1, a member arises at every step, every arising is of one of the two, and neither's activity ends); under Ends and Listed it is ever new parts, though not more of them (Generations has two active at every step). Each premise is needed: with a part whose activity never ends, the whole persists while nothing arises (Immortal); with infinitely many parts active at once, each ending at a different step, the whole persists while nothing arises, so the active parts cannot be listed finitely (Countless). The premises are consistent: generation after generation of members, each active for two steps, makes a lineage active at every step that never arises, while a new member arises at every step (Generations). The bound d is attained: members working in shifts of two steps arise only across odd steps (Shifts). The converse fails: parts arising at arbitrarily late steps, each active once, leave the whole inactive between them (Gaps). In Identity's Layered, the lineage is the whole of its members (Layered.composed). No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used.

Canonical source: [Wholes.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Wholes.lean)

<a id="前提与对应-hypotheses-and-correspondence"></a>
## Hypotheses and correspondence

- Whole is a representational premise: which formations are parts of which whole, and whether a lineage is read as the whole of its members, are supplied by the application; the whole relates to its parts only through activity, not through dependence or drawing.
- Brief d (parts are brief: none active at two steps d apart), or Ends and Listed (every part's activity ends, and at each step the active parts can be listed finitely, so finitely many are active at once): two premises, each used by one theorem. Listed is a finiteness premise, not a statement about lasting: in Countless every part ends while the whole persists and nothing arises; Brief does not say that parts end, and admits the same parts arising again (Layered).
- Identity across steps is given by the naming (identity-across-steps): the arising of parts depends on it.

The fifth independent review (I10) found that a lineage and its members are two levels of one unfolding, with the part–whole relation the one a single level of naming omits, and wrote in its §4 item 7 that a representation with a part–whole relation among formations would make it a theorem. This result gives that representation and theorem. Ren's words are “生生不息 - 一种整体的，不断创造更多生的方向” (a whole direction of unceasingly creating more 生). Where parts are brief, or end with finitely many active at once, persistence read at the level of the whole (the lineage) needs unceasing generation at the level of its members: the two levels are not alternatives, and the whole's 不息 goes through its parts' 生生 (the author's interpretation, an AI argument; K3 of the seventh independent review corrected the earlier “is” and “made of”: Whole is only coincidence of activity). Under Brief this needs only the same members arising again (Layered); under Ends and Listed it needs ever new members (needs_new); neither needs their number to grow, so “unceasingly creating more” in Ren's words does not follow from it; it does not replace Ren's words, does not show that it is good, and does not decide at which level 生生不息 is read; on Ren's delegation, at the whole's level (D5).

Contains no ethical predicate; Whole is coincidence of activity, not constitution (whole_self, Immortal.each_other), and arises_within and needs_arising use only the parts' cover (Covered); the whole relates to its parts only through activity, and its dependence, drawing and undermining are not derived from its parts'; the part relation is static, membership not changing from step to step; Brief, and Ends with Listed, are premises about the parts, which may also arise again rather than end (Layered's members); arising depends on identity across steps; the conclusion does not say which part arises, nor that their number grows; 生生不息 is read at the whole's level, on Ren's delegation; the proof is a pigeonhole, near-definitional; witnesses minimal.

- A part that never ends: the whole persists while nothing arises (Immortal.immortal). [Wholes.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Wholes.lean)
- Infinitely many parts active at once, each ending at a different step: the whole persists while nothing arises, and the active parts cannot be listed finitely (Countless.countless). - The converse fails: parts arise at arbitrarily late steps while the whole is inactive between them (Gaps.gaps). The bound d is attained (Shifts.shifts). [Wholes.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Wholes.lean)
- Whole is coincidence of activity: every formation is the whole of itself (whole_self), and two formations active at every step are each the whole of the other (Immortal.each_other). [Wholes.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Wholes.lean)
- Under Brief, generation may be the same parts arising again (Layered.brief, Layered.within, Layered.arise_again): both members of Layered are Brief 1, arises_within applies, a member arises at every step, every arising is of one of the two, and neither's activity ends.
